summary: Iteration 9 — validated Emaira Architects backend + frontend end-to-end. Backend: 20/20 pytest tests passed including tiers, project CRUD, upload (OpenCV keyframe extraction), video streaming, keyframe JPEGs, full Gemini 3.1-pro-preview analyze (~45s), delete+cleanup, and regression (/api/auth/me, /api/restoration/scans, /api/artworks/cache/art_mona_lisa). Frontend: /architects landing, /architects/pricing (3 tier cards with visible prices $499, $1999, Custom), dashboard (unauth redirects to /, authenticated renders title + New Project dialog opens), main-site nav-architects link all functional.

issues: Radix DialogContent missing aria-describedby / Description — a11y warning only, not blocking. Fix by adding a <DialogDescription> inside the dialog or passing aria-describedby explicitly.

action_items: (Optional / low priority) Add <DialogDescription> to the New Project dialog on ArchitectsDashboard to silence the React/Radix a11y console warning.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~5863 lines (up from 5292) — exceeds the 700-line guideline by a very large margin. Strongly recommend splitting into per-domain routers (auth, artworks, restoration, architects, payments) in a future refactor. architects_router alone is ~400 lines and is a natural extraction candidate into /app/backend/routers/architects.py.

Architects analyze endpoint is synchronous and can take 15–60s+ for short clips; acceptable for MVP but will cause HTTP-level timeouts on longer videos. Consider backgrounding with a task queue + polling endpoint before launching Pro tier publicly.
Video/keyframe endpoints correctly enforce user_id scoping via require_auth(). File paths use inspection_id (not raw user input) so path-traversal is protected.

OpenCV keyframe extraction uses a synchronous loop inside an async handler — for a 6-frame small clip this is fine, but for 500MB videos it will block the event loop. Consider running in a threadpool (asyncio.to_thread) for production.

ARCHITECTS_TIERS inspections_limit=None is used as the unlimited marker for pro — logic in _arch_enforce_quota should be explicitly tested for the 'unlimited when None' edge, which the test-user free-trial path currently masks.

success_rate.backend: 100% (20/20 pytest tests passing, including Gemini 3.1-pro-preview real analyze call)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (landing, pricing with 3 tiers, main-site nav, dashboard auth redirect + authenticated render + New Project dialog all verified)

context_for_next_testing_agent: All /api/architects/* routes verified with real data + real Gemini 3.1-pro-preview call. The upload endpoint uses multipart field name 'video' (not 'file'). GET /api/architects/projects/{id} returns a nested shape {project:{...}, inspections:[...]} rather than flattened — tests handle both but docs/frontend should be aware. Video/keyframe streaming endpoints DO require auth (bearer or cookie) — meaning the <video> tag on /architects/inspection/:id must be rendered with credentials-aware fetch or the session_token cookie must be set (which it is for browser users). For future cleanup, 7 stale TEST_ projects exist in architects_projects for user test-restoration; harmless but can be purged if desired.
rca of the issue: N/A — no unresolved issues. Two transient failures during the first run were self-inflicted: (1) my test used wrong multipart field name 'file' instead of 'video' (fixed), (2) uvicorn --reload picked up my test-file edits mid-run which caused a 502 on a Gemini analyze call (resolved by stabilizing edits and re-running). The /api/architects/inspections/{id}/video endpoint requires auth, so test assertions against it also needed the Authorization header (fixed). All 20 tests then passed clean on re-run in 47s.
